advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Record `Usage()` (not `cached.usage`) for a 'resumed' discovery-trace record so it matches the kernel's zero-usage convention and the inline 'made NO LLM call this run' comment.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:341-343: comment says 'A checkpoint-served chunk made NO LLM call this run — zero usage records.' then `discovery_trace.append(_trace_record(unit_plan, "resumed", cached.usage, cached))`
src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/discovery.py:444: kernel resumed outcome uses `UnitOutcome(unit_id=uid, kind="resumed", usage=Usage(), envelope=reused)` (zero usage)
unit_trace serializes `outcome.usage.as_dict()` (discovery.py:509), so the journal will carry the non-zero original usage for a resumed unit
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:347 guard is `if (not calls) and (not out):` — a too-big finding makes `out` non-empty so the guard is skipped
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:563-584: on `not produced` (context-limit at every model) a `_too_big` failure finding is appended to `out` while `calls` may be empty (all attempts raised)
commit message frames the fix as: a chunk that 'made no completed LLM call and produced no finding' is a failure — the too-big case produced a finding, so it is treated as success
advisory.finding: The 'resumed' discovery-trace record reports `cached.usage` (the original call's usage) rather than the kernel's convention of zero Usage() for a resumed outcome, diverging from review_kernel.execute_stage and risking usage double-counting if the journal is aggregated across runs.
merged_from: A P8 'too big to review' failure finding (out non-empty, calls empty) is serialized as a CheckpointEnvelope with kind='success' and checkpointed, so a genuine failure outcome is recorded/reused as a success — the false-success guard only catches the (no calls AND no out) case.
scenarios: A run that resumes checkpointed units; the journal's per-unit resumed usage is non-zero even though no tokens were spent this run.
Aggregating discovery-journal usage across resumes to estimate spend.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a chunk whose LLM call succeeds with an empty findings list is checkpointed as a reusable SUCCESS and RESUMES on a second run (chunks_resumed >= 1).
evidence: pass1.py:347 `if (not calls) and (not out):` — failure branch keyed on BOTH no-call AND no-finding

test_failed_chunk_is_not_checkpointed_and_reruns drives _FailCriteriaRunner which RAISES → pass1_with_ladder returns `([], [])` (sizing.py:524-533), i.e. exercises ONLY the (no-call, no-finding) sub-case

ABSENCE: no test uses a runner that returns `{"findings": []}` for a covered chunk and then asserts a second run RESUMES that unit (chunks_resumed >= 1) / that it is checkpointed as success — the calls-non-empty/out-empty boundary is unguarded
advisory.finding: The false-success fix's discriminating condition `(not calls) and (not out)` is only tested for the raise/no-call path; no test asserts that a chunk which made a real LLM call but produced ZERO findings is still checkpointed as a reusable SUCCESS (the legitimate clean pass the fix must preserve). A regression broadening the guard to `if not out:` would reclassify a clean zero-finding pass as a failure yet pass every existing test.
scenarios: A refactor changes the false-success guard to `if not out:` — a healthy chunk that legitimately found nothing would be reclassified failed and re-run forever, but the suite stays green
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a run_pass1 test with a FakeRunner returning {"findings": []} for a routed chunk; assert cov1 checkpoints it (discovery_trace kind 'success') and cov2 resumes it (chunks_resumed >= 1).

sizing.py:754 `if env is not None and env.digest == digest and env.is_reusable_success():`

scenarios: A misfiled or tampered checkpoint whose body carries a different digest than its path is served as if valid if the `env.digest == digest` term is dropped
